prompt: Of the three ways a change upstream shows downstream, which is the good case?

choices.text: It fails loudly
choices.why: Right. A failure is noticed and fixed.

choices.text: It carries on with a changed meaning, since nothing breaks
choices.why: No. That is the quiet, wrong case.

choices.text: It carries on and sends a new field the consumer can use
choices.why: No. That is the leaking case.

choices.text: None of them; every change downstream is bad
choices.why: No. A loud failure is the one that gets fixed.

prompt: Which half of interoperability does no file format carry on its own?

choices.text: The encoding of the characters
choices.why: No. A format can declare its encoding.

choices.text: The order of the columns
choices.why: No. A header carries that.

choices.text: What each field means
choices.why: Right. Meaning needs an agreement, not a format.

choices.text: Whether dates are valid dates in the calendar
choices.why: No. ISO 8601 handles that.

prompt: Match each part of the delivery-feed contract to what it says.
What makes a data contract more than documentation?

choices.text: Being written in the Open Data Contract Standard
choices.why: No. The format matters less than being checked.

choices.text: Being signed by both companies' lawyers
choices.why: No. A signed document still drifts if nothing checks it.

choices.text: Listing every column of the source tables
choices.why: No. It lists what is served, not what exists.

choices.text: A machine checks it against what is served
choices.why: Right. Read only by people, it drifts.

prompt: Why does the feed carry no customer name?

choices.text: Names are sensitive data under the LGPD
choices.why: No. A name is identifying, not sensitive.

choices.text: Planning routes does not need it; labels are printed in the shop
choices.why: Right. Necessity: no reason to send it every day.

choices.text: Rota Certa refused to receive personal data of any kind in a file from Ipê
choices.why: No. It receives personal data: the CEP and the order number.

choices.text: The view cannot join customers to orders
choices.why: No. It joins them for the CEP.

prompt: Under the LGPD, what is Rota Certa in this arrangement?

choices.text: A processor, following Ipê's instructions
choices.why: Right. Article 39.

choices.text: A controller of its own
choices.why: No. It does not decide the purpose.

choices.text: A data subject
choices.why: No. Data subjects are the customers.

choices.text: The DPO of Ipê
choices.why: No. That is Davi.

prompt: How many orders of 30 June 2026 went into the feed?
The only role allowed to read `share.delivery_feed` is `___`.
The contract says a field is `personal`; `gov.column_class` says its source is `sensitive`. What does the checker conclude?
hint: Which one is the source of truth for classes?

choices.text: The contract wins, since it was signed
choices.why: No. The classification is lesson 6's single source.

choices.text: Nothing; classes are informational
choices.why: No. A difference fails the check.

choices.text: One of them is wrong, and data is being sent under the wrong one
choices.why: Right. It fails until they agree.

choices.text: The field is removed from the feed automatically until somebody puts it back
choices.why: No. The checker reports; people decide.

prompt: Where should `check_contract.py` run to stop a change that breaks the contract?

choices.text: Once a month, by the DPO, as part of a review of the feeds
choices.why: No. A month of leaking is a month too long.

choices.text: Only on the consumer's side
choices.why: No. By then the data has already left.

choices.text: Inside the view, as a trigger
choices.why: No. Views do not run checks on their own definition.

choices.text: In the pipeline that deploys either side
choices.why: Right. The failed pull request is the conversation the change needed.

prompt: Put what the checker does in order.
items: Ask the database which columns it serves
Exit 0, or list the problems and exit 1

prompt: The checker fails on `full_name`. What is the right next step?

choices.text: Add `full_name` to the contract so the check passes
choices.why: No. That turns the check into a formality.

choices.text: Ask the owner whether there is a new purpose, and decide
choices.why: Right. The check forces the decision; it does not make it.

choices.text: Disable the check for this release
choices.why: No. That ships the leak.

choices.text: Rename the column to something less obvious
choices.why: No. The name is not the problem.

prompt: Why was catching the `items` change "by luck"?

choices.text: Without the cast, `count(*)` is `bigint` like `sum()`, and the check passes
choices.why: Right. Only the meaning changed, and nothing tested meaning.

choices.text: The checker skips integer columns
choices.why: No. It compares every type.

choices.text: The quality rule on items caught it, since lines and units differ on most orders
choices.why: No. Items still had at least one, so it held.

choices.text: Rota Certa reported it first
choices.why: No. The checker caught it, through the type.

prompt: Which quality rule would catch a change of meaning in `items`?
hint: Test the meaning, not the shape.

choices.text: Every item count is a positive integer
choices.why: No. Lines and units are both positive integers.

choices.text: The column `items` is never null
choices.why: No. Both versions are never null.

choices.text: The day's total equals the sum of the order items' quantities
choices.why: Right. A rule about meaning notices a changed meaning.

choices.text: The feed has as many rows as yesterday's orders
choices.why: No. The row count does not change with the meaning.

prompt: Match each change to the version it needs.

pairs.left: a new optional field at the end
a better description of a field

prompt: Rota Certa asks to keep the feed 90 days instead of 30. No code changes. What kind of change is it?

choices.text: A patch, since no field changes
choices.why: No. What is shared, and for how long, changes.

choices.text: No change at all; retention is the consumer's business
choices.why: No. Ipê is the controller and answers for it.

choices.text: A minor change, since it only adds days
choices.why: No. Privacy changes are major in this course.

choices.text: A major change, needing the owner's decision
choices.why: Right. It changes Ipê's instructions to a processor.

prompt: How is a major change to the feed published?

choices.text: By editing the view on a Friday night
choices.why: No. Every consumer breaks on Monday.

choices.text: As `delivery_feed_v2` beside the old one, until every consumer moves
choices.why: Right. Both checked, the old one removed on a date.

choices.text: By e-mailing the new schema to the consumer a week before the change goes live
choices.why: No. Without a parallel version, the consumer breaks the day it ships.

choices.text: By bumping the version number inside the same view, and keeping its name
choices.why: No. A number does not keep the old shape alive.

prompt: Why does the feed write dates as `2026-06-30`?

choices.text: ISO 8601 reads the same everywhere
choices.why: Right. A local format is read as another day without complaint.

choices.text: It is the shortest way to write a date
choices.why: No. Shortness is not the point.

choices.text: PostgreSQL cannot write dates any other way
choices.why: No. It can; the choice is deliberate.

choices.text: The LGPD requires ISO dates
choices.why: No. The law says nothing about date formats.

prompt: A spreadsheet opens the feed and the CEP `01613-005` breaks. What happened?

choices.text: The file was written in an encoding the spreadsheet did not expect
choices.why: No. An encoding breaks accents, not digits.

choices.text: The separator was a semicolon, which the spreadsheet read as part of the text
choices.why: No. The file uses commas, and CEPs have none.

choices.text: It was read as a number and lost its zero and its dash
choices.why: Right. The contract says CEPs are text.

choices.text: The CEP was encrypted
choices.why: No. The feed sends it in clear, as the contract allows.

prompt: Why is a PDF of a customer's orders not a portable format under GDPR article 20?

choices.text: PDFs are too large to send
choices.why: No. Size is not the test.

choices.text: PDFs cannot carry Portuguese characters
choices.why: No. They can.

choices.text: The law requires CSV specifically
choices.why: No. It requires structured, common, machine-readable.

choices.text: Another system cannot read its fields
choices.why: Right. Readable by a person, by no other system.

prompt: In the platform's architecture test, what plays the part of the data contract?

choices.text: The database schema
choices.why: No. Modules may not read each other's tables.

choices.text: The interface the consumer defines
choices.why: Right. And the test is the checker.

choices.text: The `platform` package
choices.why: No. That is shared code every module may use.

choices.text: A comment at the top of each file
choices.why: No. A comment is not checked.

prompt: Why was the architecture rule written before the first violation?
hint: Added later, it fails on code that ships.

choices.text: Added later, the pressure is to weaken it rather than fix the code
choices.why: Right. A rule present from the start never has to win that argument.

choices.text: Rules are cheaper to write at the start
choices.why: No. The cost is not the point.

choices.text: Go requires such a test to exist before the code of a module will compile
choices.why: No. Go requires nothing of the sort.

choices.text: There were no modules yet to test
choices.why: No. There were three.

pairs.right: what do we hold, and how sensitive?
what did we promise to whom?

prompt: What do nearly all of the course's artefacts have in common?

choices.text: They all live in OpenBao
choices.why: No. Most live in the database.

choices.text: They were all required by the LGPD in those words
choices.why: No. The law asks for outcomes, not tables.

choices.text: A decision kept as data, and a check that fails when reality disagrees
choices.why: Right. That is the whole method.

choices.text: They are all owned by the DPO
choices.why: No. Ownership is spread across roles, as lesson 9 set it.

prompt: A new law arrives next year. What does a team that keeps its decisions as data do first?

choices.text: Starts a project to find where its data is
choices.why: No. That is what a team without the tables has to do.

choices.text: Waits for the regulator to publish a tool
choices.why: No. The tables are the tool.

choices.text: Deletes everything the law might cover
choices.why: No. Retention is decided per record, with a reason.

choices.text: Queries what it already records against what the law asks
choices.why: Right. A query and a migration, not a project.
